title: `wasm target: Unit-returning cross-package wrapper leaves extra value on stack (wasm-tools validate fails)`
body:
## Description

When a function in package A calls a function in package B that wraps an `extern "wasm"` function returning `Unit`, the generated WASM wrapper function leaves an extra `i32.const 0` on the stack after the `call`, causing `wasm-tools validate` to fail with "values remaining on stack at end of block".

This occurs because MoonBit represents `Unit` as `i32(0)` in the `wasm` target. The callee already returns `i32(0)`, but the generated wrapper pushes another `i32.const 0` on top, leaving 2 values on the stack where the function type expects 1.

The bug only manifests in **cross-package calls** where the callee is not inlined. Single-package builds pass validation because the compiler inlines the call.

### Code

- Target: wasm

**`moon.mod.json`**
```json
{"name": "repro/wasm-bug", "version": "0.1.0", "source": "."}
```

**`cabi/moon.pkg.json`**
```json
{}
```

**`cabi/cabi.mbt`**
```moonbit
extern "wasm" fn mem_store32(ptr : Int, val : Int) -> Unit =
  #|(func (param i32 i32) (result i32) (i32.store (local.get 0) (local.get 1)) (i32.const 0))

pub fn write_i32(ptr : Int, val : Int) -> Unit {
  mem_store32(ptr, val)
}
```

**`main/moon.pkg.json`**
```json
{
  "is-main": true,
  "import": [{ "path": "repro/wasm-bug/cabi", "alias": "cabi" }],
  "link": {
    "wasm": {
      "exports": ["run"],
      "export-memory-name": "memory"
    }
  }
}
```

**`main/main.mbt`**
```moonbit
pub fn run(ptr : Int, val : Int) -> Int {
  @cabi.write_i32(ptr, val)
  0
}

fn main {
  ()
}
```

**Steps:**
```bash
moon build --target wasm --release
wasm-tools validate _build/wasm/release/build/main/main.wasm
```

### Environment

- OS: Linux
- OS distribution and/or version: Linux 4.4.0 (container)
- CPU Architecture: x86_64

```
moon 0.1.20260409 (a87440e 2026-04-09)
moonc v0.9.0+8a8d0e4df (2026-04-10)
moonrun 0.1.20260409 (a87440e 2026-04-09)
```

### Error output

```
error: func 3 failed to validate

Caused by:
    0: type mismatch: values remaining on stack at end of block (at offset 0x7f)
```

### Generated WASM (for reference)

```wasm
;; func 0: mem_store32 — returns i32(0) for Unit ✓
(func (;0;) (type 0) (param i32 i32) (result i32)
  local.get 0
  local.get 1
  i32.store align=1
  i32.const 0
)

;; func 3: generated wrapper — BUG: call 0 returns i32, then pushes another i32.const 0
(func (;3;) (type 0) (param i32 i32) (result i32)
  local.get 0
  local.get 1
  call 0            ;; returns i32(0) — 1 value on stack
  i32.const 0       ;; pushes another — 2 values on stack ← BUG
)
```

Expected: either `drop` before `i32.const 0`, or omit the extra `i32.const 0`.

title: moonc prove: wildcard `_` in #proof_pure match arms generates broken WhyML
body:
## Summary

When a `#proof_pure` function uses wildcard `_` in match arms for enum variants with payloads, `moonc prove` generates WhyML that omits the wildcard argument, causing Why3 to reject the output.

## Reproduction

```moonbit
// moon.pkg
options("proof-enabled": true)
```

```moonbit
// top.mbt
pub(all) enum Foo {
  Bar
  Baz(Int)
}

#proof_pure
pub fn Foo::rank(self : Foo) -> Int {
  match self {
    Bar => 0
    Baz(_) => 1   // <-- wildcard on variant with payload
  }
}
```

```
// top.mbtp
predicate is_bar(a : Foo, result : Int) {
  a.rank() == 0
}
```

```moonbit
// top.mbt (continued)
pub fn check(self : Foo) -> Int where {
  proof_ensure: result => is_bar(self, result),
} {
  self.rank()
}
```

Run `moon prove`.

## Expected

WhyML generated for `rank` should have:

```whyml
| Foo__Baz _ -> 1
```

## Actual

WhyML generated omits the wildcard argument:

```whyml
| Foo__Baz -> 1
```

Why3 rejects this with:

```
Function Foo__Baz expects 1 argument but is applied to 0
```

## Workaround

Use a named binding instead of wildcard:

```moonbit
Baz(_v) => 1   // generates correct: Foo__Baz _ -> 1
```

## Environment

- moon 0.1.20260409 (a87440e 2026-04-09)
- Why3 1.7.2
- Z3 4.13.4
- Linux x86_64

title: Windows installer download is much slower when PowerShell progress output is enabled
body:
Hi,

I found a significant performance issue in the Windows install script (`powershell.ps1`) when using `Invoke-WebRequest`.

Using the official download URL:
`https://cli.moonbitlang.cn/binaries/latest/moonbit-windows-x86_64.zip`

I measured the download time with and without progress output on **Windows PowerShell 5.1**:

```text
Testing with progress bar...
With Progress:    67.0703705 s

Testing without progress bar...
Without Progress: 7.9413672 s
```

**Observations:**
1. The progress UI slows down the download by nearly **9x** in this environment.
2. This is a well-known issue in PowerShell (see [PowerShell/PowerShell#2138](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/issues/2138)).
3. While newer PowerShell 7+ (Core) versions have better rendering performance, the **default Windows PowerShell 5.1** (which most users use for initial installation) remains heavily impacted.

**Suggested Fix:**
In `powershell.ps1`, temporarily disable `$ProgressPreference` before the download and restore it after:

```powershell
$oldPreference = $ProgressPreference
$ProgressPreference = 'SilentlyContinue'
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -OutFile $file
$ProgressPreference = $oldPreference
```

**Reproduction Script:**
```powershell
$url = "https://cli.moonbitlang.cn/binaries/latest/moonbit-windows-x86_64.zip"
$file = Join-Path $env:TEMP "moonbit-test.zip"
$sw = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()

Write-Host "Testing with progress bar..."
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -OutFile $file
$withProgress = $sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds
Write-Host "With Progress:    $withProgress s" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Remove-Item $file -Force

$sw.Restart()
$ProgressPreference = 'SilentlyContinue'
Write-Host "`nTesting without progress bar..."
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -OutFile $file
$withoutProgress = $sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds
Write-Host "Without Progress: $withoutProgress s" -ForegroundColor Green
Remove-Item $file -Force
$ProgressPreference = 'Continue'
```

title: Native target: array length silently truncated to 28 bits, causing SIGABRT for allocations >= 256MB
body:
## Summary

On the **native target**, the runtime's object header packs array/bytes length into 28 bits of a `uint32_t`. Any `Bytes`, `FixedArray`, or `String` with >= 2^28 (268,435,456) elements silently stores a truncated length. Subsequent access crashes with SIGABRT due to bounds-check failure against the wrong length.

The **wasm-gc target** is unaffected — it delegates array storage to the host VM.

## Root cause

In `moonbit.h`:

```c
#define Moonbit_make_array_header(kind, elem_size_shift, length)\
  (((uint32_t)kind << 30)\
   | (((uint32_t)(elem_size_shift) & 3) << 28)\
   | ((length) & (((uint32_t)1 << 28) - 1)))
```

The length is masked to `length & 0x0FFFFFFF` (28 bits), discarding upper bits. Meanwhile `moonbit_malloc_array` in `runtime.c` allocates the correct amount of memory via `malloc`, so the memory is there but the runtime loses track of the true length.

## Reproduction

```moonbit
// main.mbt
fn main {
  let size = 268_435_456 // 2^28 — exactly the overflow point
  let b = Bytes::make(size, 42)
  println("requested size = \{size}")
  println("actual length  = \{b.length()}")
  println("b[0] = \{b[0]}")
}
```

```
// moon.pkg
options(
  "is-main": true,
)
```

```json
// moon.mod.json
{
  "name": "repro/bytes-256mb",
  "version": "0.1.0"
}
```

### Native target (bug):

```
$ moon run src/ --target native
requested size = 268435456
actual length  = 0
RUNTIME ERROR: abort() called
main.mbt:6 at main
```

### Wasm-gc target (works correctly):

```
$ moon run src/
requested size = 268435456
actual length  = 268435456
b[0] = b'\x2A'
```

## Impact

- `Bytes.make(n, _).length()` returns wrong value for n >= 2^28
- Any read/write to such a `Bytes` crashes with SIGABRT (bounds check against truncated length)
- Silently wrong for sizes that truncate to a non-zero value (e.g., 300,000,000 → stored as 31,564,544)
- Affects all array-backed types: `Bytes`, `FixedArray`, `String`
- `FixedArray[Int]` (4 bytes/element) hits the limit at ~1GB, `FixedArray[Int64]` at ~2GB

## Environment

- `moon 0.1.20260309 (f21b520 2026-03-09)`
- Linux 6.19.6, x86_64
- Native target only; wasm-gc is unaffected

title: ICE: Key_not_found in link-core when optional Array[T] parameter has no default value (JS target)
body:
## moon version --all

```
moon 0.1.20260209 (b129ae2 2026-02-09) ~/.moon/bin/moon
moonc v0.8.2+3382e0600 (2026-02-13) ~/.moon/bin/moonc
moonrun 0.1.20260209 (b129ae2 2026-02-09) ~/.moon/bin/moonrun
moon-pilot 0.0.1-df92511 (2026-02-13) ~/.moon/bin/moon-pilot

Feature flags enabled: rupes_recta,rr_moon_pkg
```

## OS

```
Linux archlinux 6.18.7-arch1-1 x86_64
```

## Error message

During `link-core` phase:

```
Error: Moonc.Basic_hashf.Make(Key).Key_not_found(_)
```

## Root cause

The ICE is triggered by removing the default value from an optional `Array[T]` parameter in a function signature when that function is called from another package. Specifically:

```moonbit
// CAUSES ICE during link-core (js target)
pub fn Foo::new(actions? : Array[SomeExternalType]) -> Foo { ... }

// WORKS FINE
pub fn Foo::new(actions? : Array[SomeExternalType] = []) -> Foo { ... }
```

When the default `= []` is present, the linker can resolve the type. When removed (making it a plain optional), the `link-core` phase fails with `Key_not_found`.

This **only affects the JS target** — wasm-gc builds fine in both cases.

## Reproduction steps

Using [bikallem/webapi](https://github.com/bikallem/webapi) on branch `remove-default-value`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/bikallem/webapi
cd webapi
git checkout remove-default-value
cd webapi_gen && npm install && cd ..

# All of these trigger the ICE:
moon -C examples build --target js --release
cd examples && moon build notifications --target js
moon -C examples/notifications build --target js
```

### Minimal change that triggers/fixes it

In `src/notification_options_dictionary.mbt`, changing this one parameter:

```diff
- actions? : Array[NotificationAction] = [],
+ actions? : Array[NotificationAction],
```

...is sufficient to trigger the ICE. Reverting just this one line fixes it.

### Verification

```bash
# On branch main (with = [] default): builds fine
# On branch remove-default-value (without default): ICE

# Only the notifications example triggers this because it's
# the only example that calls NotificationOptions::new.
# The same pattern exists in ~15 other dictionaries.
```

## Key observations

1. **Only affects JS target** — wasm-gc builds fine
2. **Fails during `link-core` phase** — type-checking (`moon check`) passes fine
3. **Reproducible via any invocation method** — `moon -C`, `cd && moon build`, `moon -C <subdir> build` all trigger it
4. **Specific to `Array[T]` with external type parameter** — the `NotificationAction` type is defined in the same package but is an `#external` type
5. **Multiple similar patterns exist** — other `Array[T] = []` defaults were also removed (e.g., `Array[ShadowRoot]`, `Array[MessagePort]`, `Array[Touch]`, `Array[PointerEvent]`) but only trigger the ICE when their containing function is actually called from an example
6. **100% reproducible** with the steps above

## Compiler args that trigger the ICE

```
moonc link-core \
  .../core/_build/js/release/bundle/abort/abort.core \
  .../core/_build/js/release/bundle/core.core \
  examples/_build/js/release/build/.mooncakes/bikallem/webapi/webapi.core \
  examples/_build/js/release/build/notifications/notifications.core \
  -main bikallem/webapi-examples/notifications \
  -o examples/_build/js/release/build/notifications/notifications.js \
  -pkg-config-path examples/notifications/moon.pkg \
  -pkg-sources bikallem/webapi:src \
  -pkg-sources bikallem/webapi-examples/notifications:examples/notifications \
  -pkg-sources moonbitlang/core:~/.moon/lib/core \
  -target js
```

title: 文档里MoonBit for Go Programmers的位置太靠前了
body:
文档里直接把“MoonBit for Go Programmers”放到Tutorial的第二部分，而且点击页底“Next”链接会直接跳入，仿佛有点“强制阅读”的感觉，对（我这样的）新手太容易混淆了。

这带来一个巨大的假设，就是MoonBit的新手都是学过go的。

我虽然了解过一些go语言，但完全称不上熟悉。在想学习MoonBit时，刚看完“A Tour of MoonBit for Beginners”就铺天盖地地来了一波与go语言的对比，在扫视文档里的代码块时，我不得不随时切换思路，识别看到的代码是go还是MoonBit……这对于学习MoonBit来说其实阻碍挺大的。这已经是我第三次尝试开始学习MoonBit了，前两次都是在“MoonBit for Go Programmers”读到一半就烦得不行而中断了。我一度以为MoonBit的文档就是全篇建立在“和go进行对比”的基础上的……

建议将“MoonBit for Go Programmers”放到整个文档靠后些的位置，在“A Tour of MoonBit for Beginners”的末尾留一个普通链接，熟悉go的朋友可以主动选择点击阅读。但文档底部的“Next”链接最好能直接跳转到“MoonBit Language”章节，让读者快速进入MoonBit，而不是直接两种语言对比着学一遍。

title: [Bug] wasm-gc: "Invalid stub type" for closure parameters containing String or Array in FFI stubs
body:
## Description

When a wasm-gc FFI stub function takes a closure (function type) as a parameter, the compiler rejects closures whose internal signature contains `String`, `Array[T]`, or enum types with error `[4042] Invalid stub type`.

Closures passed to FFI stubs should be treated as opaque `externref` values on wasm-gc, regardless of their internal type signatures. The closure's parameter/return types are a MoonBit-level concern and should not affect the wasm import signature — the closure itself is just an externref.

**Closures that work:** those containing only `#external` types (externref) or wasm value types (`Int`, `Double`, `UInt`, etc.)

**Closures that fail:** those containing `String`, `Array[T]`, or enum types as parameters or return types

## Minimal Reproduction

`moon.mod.json`:
```json
{
  "name": "blem/closure-stub-bug",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "moonc-opt": "v0.8.1"
}
```

`moon.pkg.json`:
```json
{
  "is-main": true,
  "supported-targets": ["wasm-gc"]
}
```

`main.mbt`:
```moonbit
#external
pub type Event

#external
pub type EventListener

// --- These work (externref or wasm value types inside closure) ---

fn fail_string_return(callback : (Event) -> String) -> EventListener = "m" "g"

fn main {
  ignore(ok_externref)
  ignore(ok_no_args)
  ignore(ok_int)
  ignore(ok_double)
  ignore(ok_ret_externref)
  ignore(fail_string_param)
  ignore(fail_string_return)
  ignore(fail_array_param)
}

All FFI stubs should compile successfully. The closure parameter is an `externref` on wasm-gc regardless of its internal type signature.

title: LSP reports "Type has no method" for #cfg-gated FFI functions
body:
## Summary

The MoonBit LSP/VSCode extension reports false errors on methods that have dual `#cfg(target="...")` definitions. The code compiles successfully with `moon build` for both `js` and `wasm-gc` targets, but the LSP reports the method as unbound for one of the targets.

## Reproduction

1. Clone https://github.com/bikallem/mbt-ffi
2. Open the repo in VSCode with the MoonBit extension installed
3. Open `dom/document.mbt`
4. Observe the LSP error on line 19: `Type Document has no method document_ffi`

The relevant code pattern:

```moonbit
///|
#cfg(target="js")
extern "js" fn Document::document_ffi() -> Document =
  #| () => document

///|
#cfg(target="wasm-gc")
fn Document::document_ffi() -> Document = "webapi_Document" "new"

///|
pub fn Document::document() -> Document {
  Document::document_ffi()  // <-- LSP error: Type Document has no method document_ffi
}
```

Both `moon build --target js` and `moon build --target wasm-gc` compile successfully.

## Expected behavior

The LSP should recognize that `document_ffi` is defined under `#cfg` for both supported targets (as declared in `moon.pkg.json`) and not report an error.

## Actual behavior

The LSP appears to evaluate against a single target and does not see the `#cfg`-gated definition for the other target, reporting a false "no method" error.

## Environment

- `moon 0.1.20260209 (b129ae2 2026-02-09)`
- `moon.pkg.json` declares `"supported-targets": ["js", "wasm-gc"]`

title: Empty traits allow coercion from any type to trait object, bypassing nominal check
body:
## Summary

Empty traits (traits with no methods) do not enforce nominal trait implementation checks when coercing values to trait objects (`&Trait`). Any type can be silently coerced to `&T` for an empty trait `T`, even if the type never `impl T`.

## Reproduction

```moonbit
trait T_A {}

struct A {
  x : Int
}

impl T_A for A

trait T_B {}

struct B {
  s : String
}

impl T_B for B

fn foo(_a : &T_A) -> Unit {
  println("foo called with &T_A")
}

fn bar(_b : &T_B) -> Unit {
  println("bar called with &T_B")
}

fn main {
  let a = A::{ x: 1 }
  let b = B::{ s: "2" }
  foo(a) // OK: A implements T_A
  foo(b) // BUG: B does NOT implement T_A, but compiles without error
  bar(a) // BUG: A does NOT implement T_B, but compiles without error
  bar(b) // OK: B implements T_B
}
```

## Expected behavior

`foo(b)` and `bar(a)` should be **type errors**, since:
- `B` never declares `impl T_A for B`
- `A` never declares `impl T_B for A`

MoonBit uses nominal trait typing, so the compiler should reject coercion to a trait object unless the type explicitly implements that trait.

## Actual behavior

All four calls compile and run successfully with no errors:

```
foo called with &T_A
foo called with &T_A
bar called with &T_B
bar called with &T_B
```

## Impact

This makes empty/marker traits unusable for restricting which types are valid in a given context. Marker traits are a common pattern for encoding type-level constraints (e.g., `Send`/`Sync` in Rust), and this bug defeats that purpose entirely.

## Environment

- `moon version`: checked with latest available
- Tested on wasm-gc target

title: TCC crashes with SIGBUS when compiling large C files on ARM64 macOS
body:
## Summary

`moon test --target native` crashes with SIGBUS on ARM64 macOS when compiling large generated C files.

## Reproduction

Repository: https://github.com/mizchi/wasm5
Branch: `feat/component-model`

```bash
git clone -b feat/component-model https://github.com/mizchi/wasm5
cd wasm5
moon build --target native --debug

# Test 117 passes
moon test --target native -p moonbitlang/wasm5/test -f reference_test.mbt -i 117  # OK

# Test 118+ crashes with SIGBUS (generated C file is 454k lines)
moon test --target native -p moonbitlang/wasm5/test -f reference_test.mbt -i 118  # Exit 138 (SIGBUS)
```

## Environment

- OS: macOS
- OS version: Darwin 25.1.0
- CPU Architecture: arm64 (Apple Silicon)

```
moon 0.1.20260110 (0e584ac 2026-01-10) ~/.moon/bin/moon
moonc v0.7.1+adb125543 (2026-01-10) ~/.moon/bin/moonc
moonrun 0.1.20260110 (0e584ac 2026-01-10) ~/.moon/bin/moonrun
tcc version 0.9.28rc 2026-01-10 HEAD@cf2b37cc (AArch64 Darwin)
```

## Workaround

Compile the generated C files with clang/gcc manually instead of using `moon test --target native`.

title: Consider removing the naming rule that must start with a capital letter
body:
现在有一条规则，结构体必须大写开头，函数必须小写开头。否则将会报错，大部分语言都没有这么严格吧 我这一两年正在尝试中文代码的项目，以下是一些截图 后来改用 Rust 实现

--- 但是我尝试在 moonbit 中尝试这种命名规则，就直接报错了，我希望能考虑支持中文，不进行严格的报错 --- 延伸讨论中文编程，之前在知乎上还有个讨论 [MoonBit国产编程语言提供中文关键字的可能性有多大？](https://www.zhihu.com/question/632589892)，如果按照这个规则，那么中文是很难使用的。 为什么我会使用这种命名规则？ - 我尝试过纯中文，但是需要来回切换输入法 - 纯中文需要使用插件进行补全提示，我用过，有的太卡了，团队合作有的人不装插件，在其他没有插件的环境也不能很好的补全 - 如果使用拼音声母开头（最多4个），这些问题大大降低，中文命名也带来更多的信息，而且简短 - 为什么要用大写，因为小写的难看，不对齐 `fjy非经营`，大写`FJY非经营`，第一次看这种中文代码很扎眼，是因为中文的字高于英文字母，行高太低，显得太拥挤密密麻麻，应该调整行高

title: moonbit-lsp can not report user friendly error message, when `moon check` failed.
body:
**current behavior**

1. when `moonbit-lsp` read out of date `/target` build artifacts, `moonbit-lsp` would crash.

2. when `moonbit-lsp` can't read `/target` (/target is empty folder), `moonbit-lsp` would not work.


**expected behavior**

`moonbit-lsp` should use heuristic strategies, run `moon clean` and `moon check` to refresh out of date artifacts to solve `case 1`. when those heuristic strategies failed, `moonbit-lsp` should report user-friendly error message, and then tell user how to bug feedback.

title: moonbit-lsp and vscode extension client should serialize the log to a local filesystem
body:
**motivation**

improve bug report experience, current is hard to report bug for MoonBit vscode extension and moonbit-lsp.


**justification**

when user use `restart moonbit-lsp`, `restart vscode`, `moon clean` heuristic strategies try to fix broken state, the previous log messages would lost in vscode `MoonBit` output channel.

title: MoonBit vscode extension client should report user-friendly error message when server timeout.
body: **current behavior** **expected behavior** when server timeout to response, client can suggest user to restart `vscode` to solve issues for some common cases.

Consider this situation: 

Packages A import package B and package B depend on C and some traits in B need the data type in C.

In now situation,  packages B and A have to import the C so that the A can correctly use package B due to the dependence is not transmitted.

title: [vscode] Multiple moon.mod.json project broken with select backend
body:
In a VS Code environment, selecting a backend using "Moonbit: select backend" fails in a workspace containing multiple `moon.mod.json` files in subdirectories. This is not an issue with switching between different backends, but occurs even with a single, unified backend.

This problem arises in a common practice where an `examples` directory is created within the project to separate modules, resulting in a structure like:

- moon.mod.json
- examples/moon.mod.json

Furthermore, in this environment, the LSP's Diagnostics caches the last built `--target`, and the results of specifying a new backend are not reflected until `rm -r target` is executed.

## Actual behavior

```
notificationsAlerts.ts:42 spawn moon ENOENT
```

## Expected Behavior

Switch backend for context

Ideally, it would be desirable for each module to reflect the "preferred-target" or allow individual backend selection, but this could make the LSP implementation overly complex.

## Steps to Reproduce

```
sub/
  moon.mod.json
moon.mod.json
```

title: Moving around packages is a bit tedious & error prone
body:
For now, moving a package around requires modify all its usage across current module inside `moon.pkg.json`, although one can use search-replace & llm to perform such tedious task, but these methods are either time-consuming or prone-to-error.

I would like to suggest the following two new feature that help programmers to move their packages around:

1. Add the `Update imports` like feature as in TypeScript in IDE.
2. Add a `moon move-package a b` subcommand to update all moon.pkg.json usage of package a to point to the new location b.

`moon task` to run custom CLIs commands.
body:
Hi all👋  i'd like to suggest a "small" but useful add-on to moon CLI tool allowing devs to run custom commands directly using the `moon` CLI  tool.

**Motivation**
In several contexts we need to run custom commands and sometimes even complex or verbose composed commands using moon CLI tool and even much more (who knows?).
A standard dev practice is relying on CLI cmd automation tools like Make or Just, but they add more dependencies and more cognitive load as soon as you'll need to add environment variables and dependency rules. Sometimes, they even require you to install an other tool in a production env which isn't always a good thing.
This could be avoidable via composable CLI builder and caller directly using moon CLI tool.

**Proposal**:
a new moon task subcommand which runs custom commands, without involving external CLI automation tools like make or just. The idea is to provide a Deno task like tool, simply by adding to moon.pkg.json a tasks property. The tool should be able to read env variables, and run commands in a row using a commands queue based on declared dependencies. For instance.
```
"tasks": {
  "dev": "watchexec -r -e mbt,mod.json,pkg.json moon run cmd/main/main.mbt",
  "dev-wasmgc": "moon run --target wasm-gc ${WORK_DIR}/src/main.mbt",
  "fetch-media": {
    "command": "curl https://imgstorage.dev/"
  },
  "prod": {
    "command": "moon build --target native --release",
    "dependencies": ["fetch-media", "...whatever other depenedency"], // "moon prod" will call fetch-media and other dependencies first.
  },
}
```

Eventually this tool could be extended too, according to necessity in specific environments or integrations.

**Usage**: moon task dev, WORK_DIR=~/moon_projects/game_of_life_example && moon task dev-wasmgc, 
**Reference**: https://docs.deno.com/runtime/reference/cli/task/

title: Proposal: Add Support for `\f` Escape Sequence in String Literals

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
# Motivation

Currently, MoonBit does not support the `\f` (form feed) escape sequence in string literals. This creates an interoperability issue when working with JSON data, as JSON officially supports the `\f` escape sequence according to the JSON specification (ECMA-404).

The form feed character is a valid whitespace character in JSON and can appear in string values. When parsing JSON strings that contain `\f` sequences, MoonBit developers must currently implement manual workarounds, which is error-prone and reduces code readability.

# Benefits

Full JSON Compatibility: Supporting `\f` ensures MoonBit can seamlessly parse and generate standard JSON without unexpected errors or data corruption.

Improved Interoperability: Enables smooth data exchange with systems and APIs that generate JSON containing form feed characters.

Consistency with Other Languages: Most modern programming languages (including JavaScript, Python, Java, etc.) support `\f` escape sequences, making MoonBit consistent with industry standards.

Reduced Preprocessing: Eliminates the need for developers to manually preprocess JSON strings to remove or replace `\f` sequences before parsing.

# Current behavior 

```moonbit 
let s = "\f"
// invalid escaped character in MoonBit, But is valid in JSON 
```

[web snippet](https://try.moonbitlang.com/#426b3f79)


# Reference 

StackOverflow [How to escape special characters in building a JSON string?](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/19176024/how-to-escape-special-characters-in-building-a-json-string)

```moonbit
fn main { // scope begin

  println("do something") // exit scope
}
```

title: [Docs] Fix typo in Cascade Operator example in fundamentals.md
body:
In the file next/language/fundamentals.md, under the Cascade operator (..) section, there is a small typo in the code example explaining the operator's equivalence.

The equivalent code for the cascade example `x..f().g()` is written as `{ x.f(); x.g(); }`. This includes a redundant semicolon after the final statement, `x.g()`. This semicolon should be removed for correctness and clarity.

``` diff
--- a/next/language/fundamentals.md
+++ b/next/language/fundamentals.md
@@ -1534,7 +1534,7 @@
 the same value consecutively. The syntax is as follows:
 ```
 
 - `x..f()..g()` is equivalent to `{ x.f(); x.g(); }`.
-- `x..f().g()` is equivalent to `{ x.f(); x.g(); }`.
+- `x..f().g()` is equivalent to `{ x.f(); x.g() }`.
 
 
 Consider the following scenario: for a `StringBuilder` type that has methods
```

Regards.

Add producers custom section to moonbit Wasm binaries.

WebAssembly toolchains support a standardized producers custom section (https://github.com/WebAssembly/tool-conventions/blob/main/ProducersSection.md), which can be used by toolchains to include their compiler name and version.

## Related Issues

None found

title: Enum Overflow Issue in MoonBit Compiler with More Than 255 Elements
body:
I have discovered a bug in the MoonBit language compiler related to enumeration (enum) handling. When defining an enum with more than 255 elements, any elements beyond the 255th index overflow and incorrectly reference the earlier elements. For example:

- `Enum::E254` maps to `Enum::E254`
- `Enum::E255` maps to `Enum::E255`
- `Enum::E256` maps to `Enum::E1`
- `Enum::E257` maps to `Enum::E2`

I have tested this issue across four platforms: native, wasm, wasm-gc, and js, and have found that the problem exists on both the wasm and native platforms.

Upon reverse engineering the native implementation, it appears that the compiler reserves only one byte for the tag in the object header. Consequently, the tag's value is limited to the lower eight bits. The corresponding code is as follows:

```c
#define Moonbit_make_regular_object_header(ptr_field_offset, ptr_field_count, tag) \
  (((uint32_t)moonbit_BLOCK_KIND_REGULAR << 30) \
   | (((uint32_t)(ptr_field_offset) & (((uint32_t)1 << 11) - 1)) << 19) \
   | (((uint32_t)(ptr_field_count) & (((u

int32_t)1 << 11) - 1)) << 8) \
   | ((tag) & 0xFF))
```

I have not yet performed reverse analysis on the wasm platform's compiled output, but I suspect it may be experiencing a similar issue.

A minimal reproducible project has been packaged as a zip attachment.

[bug-poc.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20965778/bug-poc.zip)

I look forward to any guidance on how to resolve this problem or if there are plans to address it in future releases. Thank you!

# Version

title: TODO list for moonbit tour
body:
Currently, the MoonBit tour is missing some important features of MoonBit. This issue tracks which features are missing. Contribution to MoonBit tour or this list is welcomed.

Note that MoonBit tour is not intended to be a complete reference, so some less frequently used/advanced features need not be added. But many important features are currently missing, too.

Here's the list:

- [ ] generic
- [ ] trait system (including `trait`, `impl`, trait objects, `derive`, etc.)
- [ ] labelled arguments and optional arguments
- [ ] `raise` syntax and error type
- [ ] `const` syntax
- [ ] `loop` syntax
- [ ] labelled loops
- [ ] `guard` syntax
- [ ] `is` syntax
- [ ] pattern guard
- [ ] mutable field of constructor
- [ ] partial application syntax
- [ ] arrow function syntax
- [ ] pipe syntax
- [ ] infix operators and maybe operator overloading
- [ ] `letrec` syntax
- [ ] `String` and `Bytes` pattern
- [ ] JSON literal and pattern
- [ ] array view, string view and bytes view
- [ ] `typealias`, `traitalias` and `fnalias`

other stuff:

- [ ] cross reference in tour

To make it easier to use the cache elsewhere, I think it would be better to add the documentation of the release cycle in docs.

[setup-moonbit](https://github.com/moonbit-community/setup-moonbit) use Github Action to speed up install moonbit toolchain.

title: [runtime] Missing `print` Function
body:
**Description:**

Currently, the runtime of MoonBit only includes the `println` function, which automatically adds a newline character after the output. This limitation causes unnecessary line breaks for each output, which can be inconvenient for formatting or displaying multiple outputs on the same line.

**Reproduction Steps:**

1. Attempt to output text using the `println` function.
2. Notice that each call results in a new line, regardless of whether additional output on the same line is desired.

**Expected Behavior:**
It would be helpful to have a `print` function available, similar to other programming languages. This would allow output without appending an additional newline character.

**Proposed Solution:**
Implement a `print` function in the runtime that functions like `println`, but omits the newline. This would provide more flexibility in output formatting.

**Additional Information:**
If you need it, I can give you examples of how this feature would enhance usability.

Thank you for considering this improvement!

[wasm-gc] Optimizing trait polymorphism memory usage by using static tables
body:
```moonbit
trait SomeTrait {
  callback(Self) -> Unit
}

struct Value {}

impl SomeTrait for Value with callback(self) -> Unit {
  println("Value::callback")
}

fn example(value: &SomeTrait) -> Unit {
  value.callback()
}
```
```wasm
(type $SomeTrait
  (sub
   (struct
    (field  (ref $SomeTrait.method_0)))))

(type $Value.as_SomeTrait
 (sub
  $SomeTrait
  (struct
   (field  (ref $SomeTrait.method_0))
   (field  (ref $Value)))))
```
Today when using Trait polymorphism (like defining a parameter as `&Value` above) the compiler generates a new struct that's effectively a run-time vtable every time a struct that implements that trait is passed into such a function, like this:

```wasm
(call $jayphelps/example/main.example
   (struct.new $Value.as_SomeTrait
    (ref.func $@jayphelps/example/main.SomeTrait::@jayphelps/example/main.Value::callback.dyncall_as_SomeTrait)
    (local.get $value/123)))))
(; call it again or any other function which relies on trait polymorphism ;)
(call $jayphelps/example/main.example
   (struct.new $Value.as_SomeTrait
    (ref.func $@jayphelps/example/main.SomeTrait::@jayphelps/example/main.Value::callback.dyncall_as_SomeTrait)
    (local.get $value/123)))))
```

In this example, if you pass the struct value to multiple functions a new intermediate vtable struct is created each time. It's somewhat contrived given there's only one method, but hopefully it demonstrates the point cause "at scale" in complex apps with lots of methods this could add up.

Off hand I don't think there's a way around having this separate struct since Wasm GC doesn't (yet) support subtyping multiple structs, but I'm curious if this can be memory optimized by placing all the functions in a statically defined Wasm `(table)`, avoiding the overhead both of the extra allocations to store the functions? That table's index is then what you put in $Value.as_SomeTrait.

That said, this might come at the cost of CPU performance as when you need to use `call_indirect`, which incurs bounds/type checks and lookup. But I'm not sure if `call_ref` is optimized beyond `call_indirect` yet in most VMs or not. One might argue memory is cheap these days, and to error on the side of better CPU perf. I guess you could also define the vtable still using a struct with `ref.func`s but as a global, which would sort of be a middle ground perhaps. Faster calls, less redundant memory, but still some small overhead with the global lookup.

So I guess that leaves me more just curious what your thinking is around this. Mostly out of professional curiosity—you all have more compiler experience than I do, so I'd appreciate learning if this was deliberate, and why. I noticed this because my code is heavily relying on this feature, so I quickly saw a lot of redundant allocations when examining the build.

title: [Feature Request] Provide built-in support for complex number types
body:
## Why
### Cur impl
```moonbit
struct Complex[T] {
  real : T
  imag : T
}

fn main {
  let arr : Array[Complex[Float]] = [
    Complex::{ real: 1.1, imag: 2.2 },
    Complex::{ real: 1.1, imag: 2.2 },
    Complex::{ real: 1.1, imag: 2.2 },
    Complex::{ real: 1.1, imag: 2.2 },
  ]
  println(arr)
}
```
- When storing complex num in an array, since `Complex` is a heap-allocated ref type, each elem in the array actually stores a pointer to heap mem, leading to mem fragmentation and requiring secondary addressing for access, as well as hindering compiler optimizations (such as auto-vectorization).
- The overhead of passing a single Complex object by value is very small, but currently it can only be passed by reference, which introduces additional overhead such as managing reference counts and memory deallocation.

title: doc: the init and main functions should be further explained
body:
[Program entrance](https://docs.moonbitlang.com/en/latest/language/introduction.html)

Why distinguish between the init and main functions? What are the benefits of doing this? Many MoonBit beginners have these questions, but it is not explained in the documentation.

System-level initialization includes tasks such as the operating system loading the executable file, initializing processes, allocating resources, and preparing the runtime environment.

User code-level initialization includes static initializers, static fields, struct loaders, and so on.

Does the init function only include user-defined code initialization? Can the init function include system-level initialization? These points are also not clearly explained in the documentation. It would be helpful to improve this part of the documentation.

# 用例困惑

1. 中文文档，混合了英文语句
2. 提供了 make_closure 的使用途径，但是没有描述具体是什么内容与场景会使用到。

作为一个需要文档协助来入门的用户。下面这段代码给我感觉是过于抽象了。

  ```
  make_closure: (funcref, closure) => funcref.bind(null, closure)
  ```

   - funcref 是指 onclick 吗？
   - clousrs 是指 event 吗？

上面的困惑是我的猜测，可能侥幸是对的，但我也可能猜测成其他的。

3. Window onclick 这样的名称让人感觉困惑

我理解这里的是想要编写一个网页被点击时，moonbit println 的效果。

这里能否用 `CustomObj` 代替 `Window` 这样的描述。

如果关键词是 `Window`，看起来效果就是：self 关键字一定有 onclick ，甚至还有其他的 ondoubleclick。

4. 在阅读这段代码时，我想通过demo的协助来了解这段代码，但是并没有 online demo 或者链接

# 调整建议

1. 使用中文替代英文部分
2. 补充 closure 部分文档，用于介绍 make_closure
3. 修改已经存在普遍含义的关键字。

```
extern type MouseEvent
extern type CustomObj
fn onclick(self : CustomObj, e : (MouseEvent) -> Unit) = "CustomObj" "onclick"
pub fn print_hello(self : CustomObj) -> Unit {
  self.onclick(fn (_){ println("hello")})
}
```

4. 添加相应的 online demo。读者可通过链接抵达相应demo

The syntax for multi-line strings is terrible. To create a multi-line string, you have to insert a  `#|`  marker at the beginning of each line, which is overly cumbersome. Alignment for readability also needs to be considered. When copying lines from a multi-line string in the source code, you have to manually remove these redundant markers.
 
Why not adopt a syntax with two delimiters instead, like backticks, triple quotes, or even customizable delimiters?

## Expected behavior

The warn list, also documented in [warning-list](https://docs.moonbitlang.com/en/latest/toolchain/moon/package.html#warning-list), should be numbered as follows:

https://github.com/moonbitlang/moonbit-compiler/blob/main/src/warnings.ml#L1061-L1093

https://github.com/moonbitlang/moonbit-compiler/blob/main/src/warnings.ml#L768-L801

So, for the following code:

}

title: Documentation Error in Chapter `Array Pattern Match`
body:
I noticed a small issue in the documentation for the `Array Pattern Match` section. The current code snippet is as follows:

[Array Pattern Match](https://docs.moonbitlang.com/en/latest/language/fundamentals.html#array-pattern)
[数组模式匹配](https://docs.moonbitlang.com/zh-cn/latest/language/fundamentals.html#array-pattern)

```moonbit
test {
  let ary = [1, 2, 3, 4]
  let [a, b, ..] = ary
  inspect!("a = \{a}, b = \{b}", content="a = 1, b = 2")
  let [.., a, b] = ary
  inspect!("a = \{a}, b = \{b}", content="a = 3, b = 4")
}
```

However, this is incorrect. The correct version should include the `guard` keyword, like this:

```moonbit
test {
  let ary = [1, 2, 3, 4]
  guard let [a, b, ..] = ary // <---- add guard here
  inspect!("a = \{a}, b = \{b}", content="a = 1, b = 2")
  guard let [.., a, b] = ary   // <---- add guard here
  inspect!("a = \{a}, b = \{b}", content="a = 3, b = 4")
}
```

title: Linking C code in sub-packages causes errors: not find symbol `main` in the subpackage and symbol `foo` in the top package
body:
Currently some users are writing native bindings to C libraries. However, the moon build system works not so well with native backend when linking sub-packages.

Consider the pkg structure:
```
pkgMain (is-main: true, using fn `fn add(Int, Int) -> Int`)
    ^
    | provide `fn add(Int, Int) -> Int`
    |
pkgLib (is-main: false, provide binding to `int add(int, int)` in add.c)
```

We must write `link: {"cc-flags": "add.c"} ` in `moon.pkg.json@pkgMain`, not `moon.pkg.json@pkgLib`.
Otherwise:
1. symbol `main` will not be found in pkgLib (why producing an executable file rather than object file?)
2. symbol `add` will not be found in pkgMain (because in moon.pkg.json@pkgMain we don't link to add.c)

There seems to be tow question, or just one (mechanism to passing native-backend artifacts along the pkg dependency tree)?

Steps  to reproduce:
1. Clone [this repo](https://github.com/zhuguiyuan/MoonBit-BUG-Report)
2. `cd native_subpkg_require_symbol_main && make`

For someone searching Google and finding this issue:
We can use `moon run src --target native --dry-run` to see the compiling and linking process.
```bash

title: Allow exporting functions from another package for FFI
body:
# Feature Request

## Summary

Allow exporting functions from another package for FFI

## Motivation

I have two types, A and B, where A has dependency on B, and both of them have methods with the same names like "new", "toJSON', and "fromJSON". All these methods need to be exported in the FFI. Since the FFI exports only support specifying the method with the name, I moved one of the types B to a new package. But the problem is now I cannot export the methods from the B package to the A package. In the built artifacts, the dependency between A and B is gone, so I cannot use the exported methods in B package either.

<!-- Describe the problem or use case that this feature would address. Why is this feature important to you or your team? -->

## Detailed Description

It would be nice if we can specify the methods that need to be exported in the following way:

```
{
    "link": {
        "js": {
            "exports": [
                "A::new:newA",
                "B::new:newB",
                "A::toJSON:toJsonA",
                "@libB.B:toJSON:toJsonB"
            ]
        }
    }
}
```

## Checklist

- [x] I have added all necessary details to make it easy for the maintainers to understand my request.

body:
The following code results in a compiler error when targeting `native`:

```moonbit
type ExternRef

pub extern "C" fn get_ext_ref() -> ExternRef = "get_ext_ref"

fn main {
  let ext_ref = get_ext_ref()
  let arr: Array[ExternRef] = [ext_ref, ext_ref, ext_ref]
  println(arr.length())

  let arr2: Array[ExternRef] = Array::make(3, ext_ref)  // < Compiler error occurs here
  println(arr2.length())
}
```

Build command: `moon build --target native`

## Observations:

1. The error is specific to the `native` target. Building with `extern "js` and  `moon build --target js` works correctly.
2. Commenting out the `Array::make` and subsequent lines allows the code to compile successfully.
3. I guess (just I guess but I'm not sure) it is the same issue with #431 .

title: doc: error and warning list + explanation
Wrong auto-completion in the case of changing an Iterable when iterating over it
body:
# Bug Report

## Environment

### OS

Operating System: Windows

### MoonBit CLI Tools Version

```
moon 0.1.20241218 (5a38a2f 2024-12-18) ~\.moon\bin\moon.exe
moonc v0.1.20241218+f4a066f5f ~\.moon\bin\moonc.exe
moonrun 0.1.20241218 (5a38a2f 2024-12-18) ~\.moon\bin\moonrun.exe
```

## Steps to Reproduce

```moonbit
let new_connect = {}
for _, v in new_connect {
  let (members, extensions) = v
  for i4 in extensions.iter() {
    new_connect[joinTo([i4, ..members]..sort())] = (
      [i4, ..members],
      Set::of([])
    )
  }
}
```

## Expected Behavior

The `extensions.iter()` expression, it should fail to induce the full type of `new_connect`, alert that I am making changes to an Iterable when iterating over it, or accept all the code.

## Actual Behavior

Instead, the language server makes a prediction for the `iter` method when I type `extensions.` (which indicates that it guesses the type correctly), but after I accept the auto-completion, it alerts on `iter` that "Type _/0 has no method iter." The case for `members` is the same.

## Checklist

body:

```moonbit
pub(open) trait Object {

pub(open) trait Object {

title: [Feature reuest] To allow write in struct methods inside struct
Export to JS output Struct::method logic upgrade
Pipe operator |> syntax before 1.0 release
body:
MoonBit provides a convenient pipe operator |>, which can be used to chain regular function calls:
```
fn init {
  x |> f // equivalent to f(x)
  x |> f(y) // equivalent to f(x, y)

  // Chain calls at multiple lines
  arg_val
  |> f1 // equivalent to f1(arg_val)
  |> f2(other_args) // equivalent to f2(f1(arg_val), other_args)
}
```

This is from Moonbit doc, it is cool. But the syntax is not intuitive for multi-parameter functions, because the second argument is written in the first position, this is inconsistent with directly function call.  _(method call has an implicit receiver parameter which is consistent with function signature, but the pipe syntactic sugar is completely different)_

So I suggest we use `_` placeholder syntax maybe like this `x |> f(_, y)`  or `x |> f($, y)`
This also makes we can pipe to second or third parameter not only first:
```
fn init {
  debug(3.14 |> Double::to_int) // output: 3
  debug(4 |> Array::make(_, 'c')) // output: ['c', 'c', 'c', 'c']
  debug('c' |> Array::make(4, _)) // output: ['c', 'c', 'c', 'c']
}
```

_Originally posted by @bnyu in https://github.com/moonbitlang/moonbit-docs/issues/299#issuecomment-2484839716_

title: 教程中的两处问题
body:
我正在学习MoonBit，根据官方教程 [https://www.moonbitlang.cn/download/](https://www.moonbitlang.cn/download/) 搭建MoonBit环境时遇到以下两个问题：

## 问题一
### 1. 描述：
在官方教程[https://www.moonbitlang.cn/download/](https://www.moonbitlang.cn/download/) 中给出的第四步，当前面的步骤都正确执行后，在VSCode的Terminal中输入`moon new hello`会报下面这种错误：
``` 
PS D:\moonbit> moon new hello
moon : 无法将“moon”项识别为 cmdlet、函数、脚本文件或可运行程序的名称。请检查名称的拼写，如果包括路径，请确保路径正确，然后再试一次。
所在位置 行:1 字符: 1
+ moon new hello
+ ~~~~
    + CategoryInfo          : ObjectNotFound: (moon:String) [], CommandNotFoundException
    + FullyQualifiedErrorId : CommandNotFoundException 
```
### 2. 原因：
因为首次安装会改变电脑的环境变量，但VSCode只有当打开窗口的时候才会加载环境变量，所以VSCode中Terminal的环境变量还是安装前的内容，所以无法识别。

### 3. 解决方式（三种方式，目的都是重新加载环境变量）：
- 在电脑终端安装，然后打开VSCode，运行`moon new hello`命令。
- 在VSCode安装，然后重启VSCode，运行`moon new hello`命令。
- 在VSCode安装，然后在Terminal输入以下命令，重新加载环境变量，再运行`moon new hello`命令。
    > $env:PATH = [System.Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path", [System.EnvironmentVariableTarget]::Machine) + ";" + [System.Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path", [System.EnvironmentVariableTarget]::User)

## 问题二
### 1. 描述：
在官方教程 [https://www.moonbitlang.cn/download/](https://www.moonbitlang.cn/download/) 中，在正确完成前四步之后，执行第五步时会报下面的错误：
```
PS D:\moonbit\hello> moon run main
error: main is not a package
```

### 2. 原因：
 `moon run main` 这个命令可能是过时的或者错误的。

### 3. 解决方式：
根据官方给出的另一个教程：[新手之旅](https://docs.moonbitlang.cn/tour) 中给出的`moon run src/main`命令就可以正确执行。
```
PS D:\moonbit\hello> moon run src/main
Hello, world!
```

title: missing search functionality in mooncakes.io
Have you considered supporting shorthand syntax for top-level functions to return complex generic types?
body: In the Moonbit's syntax definition, it is necessary to define the types of top-level functions. This becomes tricky when a function needs to return a complex generic type. Developers are essentially unable to infer the exact return value type of this object on their own, which can be a problem when using certain libraries in Rust development. Unfortunately, Rust only solves abbreviation for trait implementations but does not address inference for struct generic types. Therefore, sometimes one has to resort to writing a long chunk of code within a function, which pollutes the true intention of the function's implementation.

l_iter.filter(fn { x => if (x & 1) == 1 { true } else { false } }).collect()

title: [Feature Request] Specify FFI export name
body:
Given that MoonBit could do FFI import already:

```moonbit
fn import_func(param: Int) -> Int64 = "extern_module" "some/function"
```

It'll be nice if a name can be specified for exports too. Conceptual grammar per [discussion](https://taolun.moonbitlang.cn/t/topic/505):

```moonbit
pub fn on_complete "ns/on_message_complete" (ptr: Int) -> Int { ... }
```

compiles to:

```wat
 (func fantix/mmhttp/h11_ffi.on_complete.fn/2
  (export "ns/on_message_complete") (param $ptr i32) (result i32)
  ...)
```

* The same type constraints apply.
* Cross-module export is unnecessary atm.

This would allow the WIT bindgen to be less [hacky](https://gitee.com/fantix/componentize-mbt/blob/f2b20a8e5322c9dd6947a05b9ddcdfaa30347e69/crates/componentize/src/lib.rs#L42-45).

title: Public function returns a ghost i32
body:
Public functions without returning types are currently compiled into WASM functions that return `i32`s:

```moonbit
pub fn no_return(a: Int, b: Int) {
  let _ = a + b
}

pub fn no_args_no_return() {
  no_return(2, 3)
}

pub fn empty_func() {
}
```

compiles to:

```wat
 (func $$username/hello/main.no_return.fn/1
  (export "username/hello/main::no_return")
  (param $a/1 i32) (param $b/2 i32) (result i32)
  (local.get $a/1) (local.get $b/2) (i32.add) (drop)
  (i32.const 0))

 (func $$username/hello/main.no_args_no_return.fn/2
  (export "username/hello/main::no_args_no_return") (result i32)
  (i32.const 2) (i32.const 3) (call $$username/hello/main.no_return.fn/1))

 (func $$username/hello/main.empty_func.fn/3
  (export "username/hello/main::empty_func") (result i32) (i32.const 0))
```

which doesn't really make sense 🤔

title: Start function or `export "_start"`?
body:
Now MoonBit is generating the following code:

```wat
 (export "_start" (func $*init*/5))
```

Looks like the WASM [Start Function](https://webassembly.github.io/spec/core/syntax/modules.html#syntax-start) is precisely the same thing:

```wat
 (start $*init*/5)
```

I can confirm the Start Function works fine on Chrome 120.0.6099.199 and wasmtime 17.0.0 (component).

Q: why do we generate `export "_start"` in the first place?

The issue here is with component model - the core wasm exports are not visible to component runtimes, I had to rewrite `export "_start"` to `start` with [a hack](https://gitee.com/fantix/componentize-mbt/blob/044441acb6b0d57015f09883e0b7f2f5019d2ab8/crates/componentize/src/lib.rs#L166-177), without which MoonBit modules couldn't initialize.

可否提供 RISC-V 二进制工具链？
body:
请问：贵项目可否提供 RISC-V 二进制工具链？

考虑到 MoonBit 工具链仅提供二进制发行且只支持 x86_64 和 AArch64 两个架构，在 RISC-V 上尝试使用 MoonBit 进行开发遇到了困难。虽然使用 Qemu 用户态模拟器可以运行 MoonBit 的相关工具，且构建示例项目时似乎行为和 x86_64 Linux 平台一致（https://github.com/moonbitlang/benchmark/issues/1 和 https://github.com/moonbitlang/benchmark/issues/1 两个工单中报告的构建问题均可复现），在运行 Hello world 时遇到了问题：

使用 `moon build` 构建 `moon new` 创建的 Hello World 项目后，在使用 Qemu 用户态模拟的 x86_64 chroot 环境中，`moon run ./main` 并没能成功运行程序，输出 `Hello, world!` 字样，而是一直没有输出地空转，期间占满 3 - 4 个处理器核心。

```
root@GreenGoo [ hello ] $ moon run ./main
Hello, world!
```

在 x86_64 设备上，该命令可以成功运行程序：

```
mingcongbai@JellyNote [ hello ] $ moon run ./main
Hello, world!
mingcongbai@JellyNote [ hello ] $
```

因此，在 RISC-V 上使用 MoonBit 存在实际上的困难。考虑到 RISC-V 设备性能正在不断提高，使用相关设备开发项目也变得现实；但是，如果必须依赖模拟器等途径运行相关工具，其性能显然会非常糟糕（也有可能因为模拟器实现上存在的问题导致其他意外）。希望贵项目可以考虑提供更多架构的二进制工具链（当然，如果可以考虑开源相关实现，就更好了）。

title: proposal for allowing braces to be optionally omitted for single statements
body: In Moonbit programming, there's an existing requirement for using explicit braces `{}` around control statements such as `break` even when they are the only statement within their scope. This is not aligned with more modern languages that allow omitting braces for single statements to reduce verbosity. I propose that Moonbit adopts a similar rule that permits the omission of braces around single statements (`break`, `continue`, `return`, etc.) when they are the only statement within braces. This change would streamline code readability and writing efficiency.

enum IntTree {
  Leaf
  Node(Int, IntTree, IntTree)
}

pub func gen_tree(n : Int) -> IntTree {
  if (n == 0) {
    IntTree::Leaf
  } else if (n == 1) {
    IntTree::Node(1, gen_tree(0), IntTree::Leaf)
  } else {
    IntTree::Node(n, gen_tree(n - 1), gen_tree(n - 2))
  }
}

pub func print_tree(self : IntTree) {
  match self {
    IntTree::Leaf => "🍁".print()
    IntTree::Node(n, l, r) => {
      "🌳(".print();
      n.print();
      ", ".print();
      print_tree(l);
      ", ".print();
      print_tree(r);
      ")".print()
    }
  }
}

pub func run() {
  while (true) {
    gen_tree(10).print_tree();
    "\n".print();
  }
}

Formatting: Big line with struct destructuring becomes syntax error
Formatting: Parenthesis being removed from logical expressions
body:
When the following is formatted:
```
idx_a == idx_b || (arg_a == arg_b && ret_a == ret_b)
```

it becomes:

```
idx_a == idx_b || arg_a == arg_b && ret_a == ret_b
``` 

Prettier transforms the non-parenthesis version to the one with parenthesis. And given the parenthesis version, prettier keeps it that way.

I like the formatting rule where expressions that combine operators of different precedence should have parenthesis.

title: Why local function's keyword is `fn` but not `func`?
body:
There was a question came up while I'm reading the repo: why local function's keyword is `fn` but not `func`?

I guess this brought some simplicity to the implementation of the language. Because a higher order procedure has to capture used local variables and make those local variables to escape if the procedure itself is escaping. This brought differences to the implementation between procedures and higher order procedures. Using two different keywords can clarify the differences between them at the beginning of the source file getting parsed.

But I think the simplicity to the end users of the language is much more important to the simplicity of the language implementation. The end users of the language has not to remember two different keywords when they are doing similar things.

Plus, if the garbage collection algorithm of the language is not automatic reference counting but a Java-like graph-based garbage collection algorithm, differing these two concepts (procedure v.s. higher order procedure) does not make more differences to the end users in their first impression which is compared to using automatic reference counting. Because if the language is using automatic reference counting as its garbage collection algorithm, the end users of the language has to annotate the ownership of the captured variable when they are using high order procedure such that they can avoid retain cycles. But a language using Java-like graph-based garbage collection algorithm does not have such an enforcement.

Of course, all these above are just my guess. It might be wrong. So why this language is using two different keywords to represent function and local function?

title: Type corresponding the WebAssembly `i64` type
body:
It seems that the `int` type is mapped to `i32` in webassembly, and `float` type mapped to `f64` (which is a little inconsistent to me). As a language targets WebAssembly, why does it not have a type corresponding `i64` type (and `f32`, too)? 

But I found this language also use two different operators `+` and `+.` for integer and float addition. So more numeric types would mean more operators for arithmatic?

One more question: why not using webassembly text mode for the "instruction" panel in the playground? I think the text mode is more readable than binary code with comments.
